children: Mortgage rates jumped in the previous week, weighing on application activity. The direction of rates in the coming weeks is expected to shape the housing market's momentum next year.
30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.28% as of November 19, up from 7.11% last week and above the average of 6.26% seen in the same period a year ago,
the Freddie Mac Weekly Mortgage Applications Survey.
15-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 6.66%, up 6.45% a week ago and 5.54% a year ago.

"While prospective borrowers often shop around for a home, they may not always think to do the same for their mortgage, as comparing multiple rate quotes can potentially save them thousands over a loan's lifetime," said Sam Khater, Freddie Mac's chief economist.

"Higher mortgage rates weighed on application activity last week," said Mortgage Bankers Association's CEO Bob Broeksmit. "Purchase applications were down 18% from a year ago, reflecting continued affordability challenges and softer homebuyer demand."
"The direction of mortgage rates in the coming weeks will be key to the housing market's momentum heading into 2027," said Broeksmit.

title: Mortgage rates jump, weighing on application activity
